SK3DNode.doc: 3D SceneKit content drawn as a flattened sprite.

SKAction.doc: An object that is run by a node to change its structure or content.

SKAttribute.doc: A specification for dynamic per-node data used with a custom shader.

SKAttributeValue.doc: A container for dynamic shader data associated with a node.

SKCameraNode.doc: A node that determines which parts of the scene are visible within a view.

SKConstraint.doc: A specification for constraining a node’s position or rotation.

SKCropNode.doc: A node that masks pixels drawn by its children so that only some pixels are seen.

SKEffectNode.doc: A node that renders its children into a separate buffer, optionally applying an effect, before drawing the final result.

SKEmitterNode.doc: A source of various particle effects.

SKFieldNode.doc: A node that applies physics effects to nearby nodes.

SKKeyframeSequence.doc: An object that performs interpolation between values specified at different times (keyframes).

SKLabelNode.doc: A graphical element that draws text.

SKLightNode.doc: A node that lights surrounding nodes.

SKMutableTexture.doc: A texture whose contents can be dynamically updated.

SKNode.doc: The base class of all SpriteKit nodes.

SKPhysicsBody.doc: An object that adds physics simulation to a node.

SKPhysicsContact.doc: A description of the contact between two physics bodies.

SKPhysicsJoint.doc: The abstract superclass for objects that connect physics bodies.

SKPhysicsJointFixed.doc: A joint that fuses two physics bodies together at a reference point.

SKPhysicsJointLimit.doc: A joint that imposes a maximum distance between two physics bodies, as if they were connected by a rope.

SKPhysicsJointPin.doc: A joint that pins together two physics bodies, allowing independent rotation.

SKPhysicsJointSliding.doc: A joint that allows two physics bodies to slide along an axis.

SKPhysicsJointSpring.doc: A joint that simulates a spring connecting two physics bodies.

SKPhysicsWorld.doc: The driver of the physics engine in a scene; it exposes the ability for you to configure and query the physics system.

SKRange.doc: A definition of a range of floating-point values.

SKReachConstraints.doc: A specification of the degree of freedom when solving inverse kinematics.

SKReferenceNode.doc: A node that’s defined in an archived .sks file.

SKRegion.doc: The definition of an arbitrary area.

SKRenderer.doc: An object that renders a scene into a custom Metal rendering pipeline and drives the scene update cycle.

SKScene.doc: An object that organizes all of the active SpriteKit content.

SKShader.doc: An object that allows you to apply a custom fragment shader.

SKShapeNode.doc: A mathematical shape that can be stroked or filled.

SKTexture.doc: An image, decoded on the GPU, that can be used to render various SpriteKit objects.

SKTextureAtlas.doc: A collection of textures optimized for storage and drawing performance.

SKTileDefinition.doc: A single tile that can be repeated in a tile map.

SKTileGroup.doc: A set of tiles that collectively define one type of terrain.

SKTileGroupRule.doc: Rules that describe how various tiles should be placed in a map.

SKTileSet.doc: A container for related tile groups.

SKTransformNode.doc: A node that allows its children to rotate in 3D.

SKTransition.doc: An object used to perform an animated transition to a new scene.

SKUniform.doc: A container for uniform shader data.

SKVideoNode.doc: A graphical element that plays video content.

SKView.doc: A view subclass that renders a SpriteKit scene.

SKWarpGeometry.doc: A definition for a deformation of nodes that conform to SKWarpable.

SKWarpGeometryGrid.doc: A definition for a grid-based deformation of nodes that conform to SKWarpable.

SKPhysicsContactDelegate.doc: Methods your app can implement to respond when physics bodies come into contact.

SKSceneDelegate.doc: Methods that, when implemented, allow any class to participate in the SpriteKit render loop callbacks.

SKViewDelegate.doc: Methods to take custom control over the view’s render rate.

SKWarpable.doc: A protocol for objects that can be warped and animated by an SKWarpGeometry.

SKActionTimingMode.doc: The modes that an action can use to adjust the apparent timing of the action.

SKActionTimingEaseIn.doc: Specifies ease-in pacing. Ease-in pacing causes the animation to begin slowly and then speed up as it progresses.

SKActionTimingEaseInEaseOut.doc: Specifies ease-in ease-out pacing. An ease-in ease-out animation begins slowly, accelerates through the middle of its duration, and then slows again before completing.

SKActionTimingEaseOut.doc: Specifies ease-out pacing. Ease-out pacing causes the animation to begin quickly and then slow as it completes.

SKActionTimingLinear.doc: Specifies linear pacing. Linear pacing causes an animation to occur evenly over its duration.

SKAttributeType.doc: Options that specify an attribute’s data type.

SKBlendMode.doc: The modes that describe how the source and destination pixel colors are used to calculate the new destination color.

SKBlendModeAdd.doc: The source and destination colors are added together.

SKBlendModeAlpha.doc: The source and destination colors are blended by multiplying the source alpha value.

SKBlendModeMultiply.doc: The source color is multiplied by the destination color.

SKBlendModeMultiplyX2.doc: The source color is multiplied by the destination color and then doubled.

SKBlendModeReplace.doc: The source color replaces the destination color.

SKBlendModeScreen.doc: The source color is added to the destination color times the inverted source color.

SKBlendModeSubtract.doc: The source color is subtracted from the destination color.

SKInterpolationMode.doc: The modes used to interpolate between keyframes in the sequence.

SKInterpolationModeLinear.doc: Values between two keyframes are interpolated linearly.

SKInterpolationModeSpline.doc: Values between two keyframes using a spline curve.

SKInterpolationModeStep.doc: Values between two keyframes are not interpolated. Instead, the value is that of the most recent keyframe.

SKLabelHorizontalAlignmentModeCenter.doc: Centers the text horizontally on the node’s origin.

SKLabelHorizontalAlignmentModeLeft.doc: Positions the text so that the left side of the text is on the node’s origin.

SKLabelHorizontalAlignmentModeRight.doc: Positions the text so that the right side of the text is on the node’s origin.

SKLabelVerticalAlignmentModeBaseline.doc: Positions the text so that the font’s baseline lies on the node’s origin.

SKLabelVerticalAlignmentModeBottom.doc: Positions the text so that the bottom of the text is on the node’s origin.

SKLabelVerticalAlignmentModeCenter.doc: Centers the text vertically on the node’s origin.

SKLabelVerticalAlignmentModeTop.doc: Positions the text so that the top of the text is on the node’s origin.

SKNodeFocusBehavior.doc: Options for the focusable states of a SpriteKit node.

SKNodeFocusBehaviorFocusable.doc: Node is focusable and prevents nodes that it visually obscures from becoming focusable.

SKNodeFocusBehaviorOccluding.doc: Node is not focusable and prevents nodes that it visually obscures from becoming focusable.

SKParticleRenderOrder.doc: The order to use when the emitter’s particles are rendered.

SKParticleRenderOrderDontCare.doc: The particles can be rendered in any order. SpriteKit may choose to reorder the particles to improve rendering performance.

SKParticleRenderOrderOldestFirst.doc: The particles are rendered from oldest to newest.

SKParticleRenderOrderOldestLast.doc: The particles are rendered from newest to oldest. This is the default value.

SKRepeatMode.doc: The modes used to determine how the sequence repeats.

SKRepeatModeClamp.doc: When a sample is calculated, the time value is clamped to the range of time values found in the sequence. For example, if the last keyframe’s time value is 0.5, a sample at any time value from 0.5 to 1.0 returns the last keyframe’s value.

SKRepeatModeLoop.doc: When a sample is calculated, the sequence loops back to the beginning of the sequence. For example, if the last keyframe’s time value is 0.5, then a sample at any time value from 0.5 to 1.0 returns the same value as the sequence did from 0.0 to 0.5.

SKSceneScaleMode.doc: The modes that determine how the scene’s area is mapped to the view that presents it.

SKSceneScaleModeAspectFill.doc: The scaling factor of each dimension is calculated and the larger of the two is chosen. Each axis of the scene is scaled by the same scaling factor. This guarantees that the entire area of the view is filled but may cause parts of the scene to be cropped.

SKSceneScaleModeAspectFit.doc: The scaling factor of each dimension is calculated and the smaller of the two is chosen. Each axis of the scene is scaled by the same scaling factor. This guarantees that the entire scene is visible but may require letterboxing in the view.

SKSceneScaleModeFill.doc: Each axis of the scene is scaled independently so that each axis in the scene exactly maps to the length of that axis in the view.

SKSceneScaleModeResizeFill.doc: The scene is not scaled to match the view. Instead, the scene is automatically resized so that its dimensions always match those of the view.

SKTextureFilteringMode.doc: Texture filtering modes to use when the texture is drawn in a size other than its native size.

SKTextureFilteringLinear.doc: Each pixel is drawn by using a linear filter of multiple texels in the texture. This mode produces higher quality results but may be slower.

SKTextureFilteringNearest.doc: Each pixel is drawn using the nearest point in the texture. This mode is faster, but the results are often pixelated.

SKTileAdjacencyMask.doc: An enumeration defining how neighboring tiles are automatically placed next to each other.

SKTileDefinitionRotation.doc: The allowed rotations for a given tile.

SKTileSetType.doc: An enumeration defining how tiles are arranged.

SKTransitionDirection.doc: For some transitions, the direction in which the transition is performed.

SKUniformType.doc: An enumerated type to identify the type of a uniform object.

SKUniformTypeFloat.doc: Indicates that the uniform variable holds a 32-bit floating-point value.

SKUniformTypeFloatMatrix2.doc: Indicates that the uniform variable holds a 2 x 2 matrix of four 32-bit floating-point values.

SKUniformTypeFloatMatrix3.doc: Indicates that the uniform variable holds a 3 x 3 matrix of four 32-bit floating-point values.

SKUniformTypeFloatMatrix4.doc: Indicates that the uniform variable holds a 3 x 3 matrix of four 32-bit floating-point values.

SKUniformTypeFloatVector2.doc: Indicates that the uniform variable holds a vector of two 32-bit floating-point values.

SKUniformTypeFloatVector3.doc: Indicates that the uniform variable holds a vector of three 32-bit floating-point values.

SKUniformTypeFloatVector4.doc: Indicates that the uniform variable holds a vector of four 32-bit floating-point values.

SKUniformTypeNone.doc: Indicates that the uniform variable does not currently hold any data. A uniform object has this type until the first time its value is set.

SKUniformTypeTexture.doc: Indicates that the uniform variable holds a reference to a SpriteKit texture.
